$schemaNote: v2 of the Vibes contract. A variant states a palette; primal/theme/tokenMap.ts states how that palette becomes a colour theme. Nothing reads this file at runtime - src/vs/workbench/contrib/primalVibes mirrors the ids and labels by hand, and must stay in sync.
$seedIsFlat: Every key of `seed` and `surfaces` is a slot id in tokenMap.ts, spelled identically. There is no name mapping: seed.ansiBrightCyan fills slot "ansiBrightCyan".
$semanticsAreAbsent: error, warning, info, added, untracked, deleted, modified, conflict and the six diff-wash slots are DELIBERATELY not in a seed. The owner is colour blind (amber reads as green), so these must be separated by LIGHTNESS, not hue. A seeded hex cannot promise that; a synthesised one can be measured. primal/theme/generateTheme.ts places each role at the first lightness that measures at least validateTheme's own 11 dE00 from every role already placed, under normal, protanopic, deuteranopic and tritanopic vision, on the emitted hex - and for the roles a red-green deficiency collapses together (warning, error, added, conflict, deleted) it additionally requires that distance from lightness alone. Do not add them here. The values the six original vibes used BEFORE this landed are recorded as the expected output of the map path in primal/theme/tokenMap.test-fixture.json; the themes they ship today are generated.
$ansiBlackIsLifted: ansiBlack and ansiBrightBlack in the four dark vibes are NOT the values they were hand-authored with. They were the border and the muted ink - one plane off the editor - which put ANSI black at 1.21:1 (basalt), 1.29:1 (dusk), 1.37:1 (fern) and 1.37:1 (tide) against terminal.background: SGR 30 printed text nobody could read, and validateTheme.ts calls that an error. Each black now sits at the 3.0:1 ANSI floor, moved along OKLab L holding its hue and chroma, so it is the same colour lifted rather than a different one; each bright black was then pushed until a trichromat can tell the pair apart (>= 10 dE00, the validator's ANSI ramp threshold). Black is still the darkest of the sixteen in every vibe, which is the part of the convention a program can rely on. importPalette.ts applies the identical rule to every corpus palette; see its ANSI_MIN_CONTRAST and ANSI_MIN_SEPARATION.
$ansiRampIsSeparated: The sixteen ANSI slots must be sixteen colours a TRICHROMAT can resolve, not sixteen hex values. validateTheme.ts asks for 10 dE00 between every one of the 120 pairs; the hand-authored ramps did not hold it, and the failure was invisible because the check filed a collision under whichever observer scored lowest - simulating a dichromat almost always shrinks a distance, so every trichromat collision was labelled "inherent to the ANSI standard" and demoted to a warning. Measured properly the six vibes carried 49 trichromat collisions between them: Tide painted ansiGreen #7FC79C and ansiBrightGreen #9CD8B4 5.47 dE00 apart, Dusk put ansiWhite 5.42 from ansiBrightMagenta, Fern put ansiYellow 5.32 from ansiBrightYellow. 46 of the 96 ANSI slots below were therefore moved along OKLab L - hue held to within 4 degrees, chroma held or raised but never cut, so nothing is on its way to grey and ANSI red is still red - by at most 0.10 L, until every pair clears 10 dE00 (worst pair now: ink 10.12, basalt 10.05, tide 10.04, dusk 10.05, fern 10.06, ridge 10.03), every slot still clears the 3.0:1 ANSI floor, and ansiBlack is still the darkest of the sixteen. The moved values are the ones below; primal/theme/tokenMap.test-fixture.json and the six shipping themes were regenerated from them, not hand-edited.
$surfacesArePinned: `surfaces` holds the chrome planes a palette corpus never supplies (elevated, hover, input, tab, control border, muted/disabled/subtle ink, bright accent). All six vibes pin all of them, because these were eyeballed when the themes were hand-written and NO mix of seed colours reproduces them exactly. tokenMap.ts carries approximate fallbacks, with their measured error, for palettes that omit them.

depthBands.$comment: Descriptive band for how far the chrome plane sits off the editor plane, measured as |HSL lightness difference| between seed.editorBg and seed.chromeBg. The seed pins the actual planes; depth only picks the fallback strength for unpinned surfaces.

rules: Meaning is never encoded in hue alone (owner is colour blind): errors/warnings pair colour with icon shape and text, and semantic colours are separated by lightness.
Diff/error/warning semantic colours stay near VS Code conventions for familiarity, tinted toward the vibe.
A family whose accent equals its editor foreground is monochrome; it carries syntax structure in weight (syntaxEmphasis "weight") rather than hue.
